$comment: The standing prediction sheet. Ten statements tied to graph records, each with a date and a resolution rule, so that different predictors (frontier models, researchers) answer the same questions and can be compared when the dates arrive. Register answers with scripts/predict.mjs; they are locked in the public event log and shown at #/predictions. Add a statement only with a resolution rule a stranger could apply.

statements.subject: hrm:question/en1-inhibition-translates-to-human-skin
statements.statement: By 2028-12-31, a peer-reviewed primary study reports that YAP inhibition (verteporfin or another agent) produces regeneration with hair follicles in a porcine full-thickness wound model.
statements.resolutionCriteria: Resolves YES if a primary research paper (not a review or preprint) in a peer-reviewed journal reports histologically confirmed hair follicles in treated porcine full-thickness wounds and their absence or reduction in controls. Preprints, mouse-only data, and conference abstracts do not count.

statements.subject: hrm:capability/pharmacological-scar-reduction-in-humans
statements.statement: By 2028-12-31, a randomised controlled trial of verteporfin for scar reduction in human wounds reports that its registered primary scar endpoint was met.
statements.resolutionCriteria: Resolves YES if a registered RCT (ClinicalTrials.gov or equivalent) of verteporfin in human wounds reports, in a peer-reviewed paper or a posted results record, a statistically significant improvement on the primary scar endpoint as registered before unblinding. Secondary endpoints or open-label series do not count.

statements.subject: hrm:question/partial-reprogramming-human-safety
statements.statement: By 2027-12-31, a Phase 1 trial of partial epigenetic reprogramming in humans (for example ER-100, OSK) reports completed dosing with no dose-limiting toxicity and no treatment-related tumour.
statements.resolutionCriteria: Resolves YES if the sponsor, a registry results record, or a peer-reviewed paper reports that a Phase 1 partial-reprogramming trial completed its planned dosing cohorts with no dose-limiting toxicity and no treatment-attributed neoplasm. A trial paused or halted for safety, or with no public safety readout by the date, resolves NO.

statements.subject: hrm:question/pluripotent-derived-skin-engrafts-in-humans
statements.statement: By 2029-12-31, a skin graft derived from pluripotent stem cells and carrying hair follicles is transplanted into a person in a registered clinical trial.
statements.resolutionCriteria: Resolves YES if a registered trial (any phase) reports at least one participant transplanted with a pluripotent-stem-cell-derived graft that contains hair follicles at transplant, confirmed by the trial's own description or a peer-reviewed report. Grafts without appendages, or adult-stem-cell grafts, do not count.

statements.subject: hrm:question/wound-induced-hair-neogenesis-in-human-skin
statements.statement: By 2028-12-31, de novo hair follicle formation after wounding in adult human skin is reported in a peer-reviewed paper, in vivo or in a human skin xenograft, with histological or lineage confirmation.
statements.resolutionCriteria: Resolves YES if a peer-reviewed primary paper reports new hair follicles forming within the wound bed of adult human skin (in a person or a human skin xenograft), confirmed by histology or lineage tracing, and distinguished from follicles that survived at the wound edge. Mouse data and organoid-only data do not count.

statements.subject: hrm:question/gene-corrected-epidermal-graft-long-term-safety
statements.statement: By 2028-12-31, a peer-reviewed follow-up of at least five years after transplantation of gene-corrected autologous epidermal stem-cell grafts reports no clonal expansion of concern and no malignancy in the grafted skin.
statements.resolutionCriteria: Resolves YES if a peer-reviewed paper reports at least five years of follow-up in one or more recipients of gene-corrected epidermal stem-cell grafts with integration-site or clonal analysis and no malignancy in grafted skin. A report of malignancy, or no five-year report by the date, resolves NO.

statements.subject: hrm:question/topical-gene-delivery-generalises-beyond-eb
statements.statement: By 2028-12-31, a topical HSV-vector gene therapy for a skin indication other than epidermolysis bullosa reports that its registered primary endpoint was met in a Phase 2 or later trial.
statements.resolutionCriteria: Resolves YES if a registered Phase 2 or Phase 3 trial of a topically applied HSV-based gene therapy for a non-epidermolysis-bullosa indication reports meeting its primary endpoint, in a peer-reviewed paper, a registry results record, or a sponsor announcement with the endpoint data. Phase 1 safety-only readouts do not count.

statements.subject: hrm:question/organised-microvasculature-in-thick-regenerated-tissue
statements.statement: By 2029-12-31, an engineered dermal construct more than 2 mm thick with a prevascularised, hierarchically organised vessel network is shown perfused and stable for at least 12 weeks in a large animal, in a peer-reviewed paper.
statements.resolutionCriteria: Resolves YES if a peer-reviewed primary paper reports a dermal or skin construct with stated thickness above 2 mm, vessels of more than one calibre connected to host circulation, perfusion demonstrated by imaging or histology, and persistence at 12 weeks or more in a pig, sheep or non-human primate. Rodent models do not count.

statements.subject: hrm:question/why-avotermin-phase-3-failed
statements.statement: By 2027-12-31, the full Phase 3 results of avotermin (TGF-β3, Juvista) are published in a peer-reviewed journal or posted to a registry with primary endpoint data.
statements.resolutionCriteria: Resolves YES if a peer-reviewed paper or a registry results record presents the Phase 3 primary endpoint data for avotermin, including the numbers behind the failure. Press releases and secondary summaries do not count.

statements.subject: hrm:question/dermal-adipocyte-regeneration-in-human-wounds
statements.statement: By 2028-12-31, conversion of myofibroblasts to adipocytes is demonstrated in human wound tissue, in vivo or in ex-vivo human skin, in a peer-reviewed paper with lineage evidence.
statements.resolutionCriteria: Resolves YES if a peer-reviewed primary paper shows, with lineage tracing or an equivalent clonal method, that cells of myofibroblast origin become adipocytes in human wound tissue (in a person, a human skin xenograft, or ex-vivo human skin). Mouse-only data and correlative marker co-expression do not count.
